newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut Byblos bank to issue EuroCDs, raise capital.
newsitem.headline: Beirut Byblos bank to issue EuroCDs, raise capital.

text.p: BEIRUT, March 20 (reuter) - Shareholders in Lebanon's Byblos Bank approved on Thursday a three-year $300 million EuroCD programme and the bank's 1996 financial results.
They also approved a 250 Lebanese pounds ($0.16) net dividend and a 17.6 billion pounds capital increase, part of a plan to raise the bank's capital to $200 million.
A shareholders' meeting agreed to issue the first $100 million tranche of the EuroCDs in May.
The notes will have five-year maturities and carry between 2.2 and 2.4 percent interest plus the interest on U.S. treasury bonds, Byblos Assistant general manager Moussa Makssoud told Reuters.
The issue would be managed by Merrill Lynch in association with the Dutch bank ABN AMRO, he said.

The bank's borrowing programme continues a trend by Lebanese banks towards international fund-raising which began last year when five banks including Byblos raised a total of $420 million on international debt markets.
Bankers and economists said last year that Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri was urging Lebanon's comercial banks to raise $800 million-$1 billion abroad by mid-1997.

The shareholders at the bank, which ranked fifth among Lebanon's 82 banks in 1996 in size of customer deposits, also approved the allocation of 10.626 billion pounds as dividend out of the bank's 1996 net income of 37.500 billion pounds, Maksoud said.
According to the bank's annual results, profits rose 60 percent in 1996 while total assets rose 38 percent to $1.43 billion.

The assembly approved the allocation of 3.750 billion pounds to legal reserves, 1.560 billion pounds to regulatory banking risk reserve, 21 billion pounds to general reserves and 564 million pounds in balance carried forward, he added.
"The 250 Lebanese pound dividend (per share) will be distributed as of the beginning of next week," Maksoud said.
At an extraordinary session held later on Thursday, the shareholders approved the first phase of an ambitious plan to raise capital to $200 million.

"The shareholders agreed to raise the bank's capital to 66.074 billion Lebanese pounds ($42.7 million) from 48.454 billion pounds through the distribution of 14,683,200 new shares to existing shareholders," Maksoud said.
This raised the bank's total equity to 162.548 billion pounds, he added.
Shareholders will have the right to subscribe to four new shares for every 11 shares they hold. The nominal price of the new shares is 1,200 Lebanese pounds.
($1= 1,552 Lebanese pounds at the end of 1996)
